title: Custom Post Type 404 Errors
description: Fix custom post types and taxonomies returning 404 — rewrite rules, flush conflicts, and registration order issues.

steps.title: Identify Which CPT/Taxonomy 404s
steps.instructions: Note if single posts, archives, or both return 404. List the post type slug and whether it is registered by theme, plugin, or ACF/CPT UI.

steps.title: Flush Permalink Rewrite Rules
steps.instructions: Visit Settings → Permalinks and save. CPTs registered after last flush will 404 until rules regenerate. Re-activate registering plugin if needed.

steps.title: Check Rewrite Slug Conflicts
steps.instructions: CPT slug may conflict with a page slug, category, or another CPT. Change rewrite slug in registration args or rename conflicting page.

steps.title: Verify has_archive and publicly_queryable
steps.instructions: CPT registration needs 'has_archive' => true for archive pages and 'publicly_queryable' => true for front-end access. Check register_post_type() args.

steps.title: Fix Registration Hook Priority
steps.instructions: CPTs must register on init hook. Registering too late or on wrong hook means rewrite rules never include them. Check theme functions.php and plugin load order.

steps.title: Sync ACF or CPT UI Settings
steps.instructions: If using ACF Post Types or Custom Post Type UI, confirm settings saved and JSON synced. Re-save CPT settings and flush permalinks again.

steps.title: Check for Rewrite Rule Conflicts
steps.instructions: SEO plugins, multilingual plugins, and custom permalink plugins may override CPT rules. Test with SEO plugin permalink settings disabled temporarily.

steps.title: Verify Single and Archive URLs
steps.instructions: Test single CPT post URL and archive URL. Confirm pagination on archive works. Document CPT slugs for client reference.
